why_hard: The referral letter frames this as ischemic cardiomyopathy because of the father's MI. The patient's own record shows nonobstructive coronaries and a resuscitated VF arrest, so the ICD is for secondary prevention.

pages.title: PCP referral letter
lines: I am referring Mr. Achterberg for ICD consideration. He has a cardiomyopathy with EF in the low 30s and a very strong family history of premature coronary disease - his father had an MI at 49 and later died of ischemic cardiomyopathy, and a paternal uncle had CABG at 55. I suspect ischemic cardiomyopathy. He has been wearing a LifeVest since the spring.
He also has HTN, OSA on CPAP, and obesity (BMI 34).

pages.title: EP consultation
lines: HPI: On 03/08/2026 pt collapsed while on a treadmill at his gym. Bystander CPR, AED analyzed VF and delivered 1 shock with ROSC. Emergent cath that day showed nonobstructive CAD, no culprit, no intervention. Troponin peak attributed to arrest/CPR, no MI. CMR 03/11: LVEF 31%, patchy mid-wall LGE, no myocarditis by T2. No reversible cause found (K, Mg normal, no drugs, no QT prolongation). Neurologically intact on discharge, no anoxic injury. Discharged 03/14 with wearable defibrillator and GDMT. No WCD shocks since.
Now: mild DOE on hills and stairs. NYHA class II. No syncope.
FHx: father MI at 49 and died of ischemic CM; paternal uncle CABG. No family SCD.
Assessment: Resuscitated VF arrest without reversible cause, with persistent LV dysfunction. Coronaries nonobstructive - not ischemic CM despite family history.
Indication: SECONDARY prevention ICD (survivor of VF cardiac arrest).
Plan: transvenous single-chamber ICD; SDM visit; admit.

pages.title: Cardiac catheterization report
lines: HARBORVIEW MEDICAL CENTER - EMERGENT CARDIAC CATH
LM: normal. LAD: 30% mid. LCx: 20% OM1. RCA: minor irregularities.
Conclusion: Nonobstructive CAD. No PCI performed.

pages.title: Echocardiogram report
lines: LVIDd 6.0. Global hypokinesis, no regional WMA.
RV normal. No significant valve disease.
Compared to CMR 03/2026 (31%): no meaningful change.

pages.title: Shared decision making visit
lines: Harborview EP - Shared Decision Making Encounter
Tool: evidence-based ICD decision aid (video + booklet).
We reviewed recurrence risk after VF arrest, how the ICD treats VF, risks of implant, inappropriate shocks, driving rules, and that the LifeVest is not a long-term option.

pages.title: Pre-admission plan
lines: Supporting factors: severe OSA (AHI 46) on CPAP - post-sedation monitoring; obesity BMI 34 w/ difficult airway history; HTN; transition off WCD requires telemetry until device check POD1.
Limiting conditions: none. Neuro intact, no terminal illness, sinus rhythm (no AF), clinically stable.

value: severe obstructive sleep apnea on CPAP
comorbidities.why: Supporting factors on the pre-admission plan.

lvef_percent.why: CMR 03/11/2026 31%; TTE 09/12/2026 33%. The later one wins.

cardiomyopathy_type.why: EP states the indication is secondary prevention after a resuscitated VF arrest, with nonobstructive coronaries. Per the definitions, a request resting on prior cardiac arrest is 'other'. The PCP's 'suspect ischemic' rests on the father's history, not the patient's.

recent_mi_revasc.why: Cath 03/08/2026: no PCI; troponin rise 'no MI'; page 8 'No MI, PCI or CABG.'

optimal_medical_therapy_months.why: Metoprolol, ARNI and MRA since 2026-03-12, about 7.3 months to the implant.

shared_decision_making.why: SDM 09/24/2026 with an evidence-based decision aid.

limiting_conditions.why: 'Limiting conditions: none. Neuro intact' (no anoxic brain injury).

action_reasoning: Rule 1: the request rests on a prior cardiac arrest, so cardiomyopathy_type is 'other' and a physician must decide. All other facts are present (and would otherwise pass). Escalate.
